location: Valley County, Idaho, USA (remote; Stibnite mining district)
selection_note: Hindsight-selected development case (not a sealed holdout). Chosen because the SEC EDGAR record gives machine-readable acceptance timestamps for a feasibility/power-plan signal (Jan 2022), the permit decision (Jan 2025) and a utility grid-upgrade equipment agreement (Feb 2025, recorded as a later event, not a target). Selected knowing the outcome.

signals.title: Grid power selected as primary supply; 60 MW load requires upgrading ~63 mi of Idaho Power lines to 138 kV

availability_evidence.note: SEC EDGAR acceptance datetime 2022-01-03T13:32:59+00:00 (UTC, from data.sec.gov submissions API acceptanceDateTime for accession 0001104659-22-000158); same filing as s1

signals.source_quote:
Grid power was selected
as the preferred primary power supply for the Project based on its low operating cost, low unit prices, and Idaho Power Company’s
existing clean energy portfolio. The existing grid network would need to be upgraded to provide the power necessary to support
the 60-megawatt ( **MW**) load.

later_procurement_events:
2025-02-13 (8-K accepted 2025-02-13T22:29:39Z per the submissions API, agent-asserted; capture perpetua-stibnite-8k-ipco-20250213): agreement with Idaho Power Company for long-lead grid-upgrade equipment. Exact text: 'On February\xa013, 2025, Perpetua entered into
an agreement with Idaho Power Company (“IPCo”) to begin procurement of long lead equipment required to increase the electrical
capacity to the plant.\xa0 This is an important step to ensure parts are available for installation under a future construction agreement.
Under the terms of the agreement, Perpetua is responsible for paying all costs incurred by IPCo as they procure new equipment from vendors
with an estimated cost of $90.2 million.'
